Narrative: The II:8998932 G>A splice-acceptor variant in tdp-1 is a high-impact change likely to produce loss of TDP-1 function. TDP-1 is an RNA-binding protein expressed in neurons and required for normal RNA splicing and neuronal maintenance; loss could misregulate transcripts that specify AMso asymmetric division or the glia→MCM fate conversion [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].
rationale: A high-impact splice-acceptor variant in tdp-1 (RNA-binding protein TDP-43 ortholog) is likely to produce a strong loss-of-function that can broadly disrupt RNA splicing and neuronal gene expression required for AMso asymmetric division and male neuronal maturation; TDP-1 is expressed in neurons and has established roles in neuronal biology in C. elegans [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].

Narrative: V:20636314 A>T affects a splice-donor in ttr-13, a predicted cell-surface protein; a high-impact splice change could abolish or alter a surface protein needed for intercellular signaling that instructs AMso asymmetric division [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: A high-impact splice-donor variant in ttr-13 (predicted cell-surface protein) could perturb a cell-surface or signaling molecule necessary for AMso division asymmetry or for the glia-to-neuron fate switch in males. Although the gene lacks curated functional literature here, the splice_donor high-impact class increases prior likelihood that it affects AMso behavior [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: I:9982115 C>T is a missense in sys-1, a core effector of Wnt/ß-catenin asymmetry pathways that directly pattern asymmetric neuroblast division and diversify sensory lineages; a damaging change could disrupt the asymmetric division of AMso that produces MCMs during male maturation [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19389360, 21917811, 29962933].
rationale: sys-1 is a known beta-catenin–type effector in Wnt asymmetry pathways that directly regulate asymmetric neuroblast divisions and cell-fate diversification; a missense change could perturb SYS-1 activity during the male-specific AMso asymmetric division that produces MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19389360, 21917811, 29962933].

Narrative: IV:5537852 G>A is a missense in fem-1, a component of male sex-determination and Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase biology; altered FEM-1 function can perturb male somatic differentiation programs and could plausibly prevent the male-specific AMso division or the subsequent MCM fate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].
rationale: fem-1 is part of male somatic and germline sex-determination pathways and participates in ubiquitin-mediated regulation; a missense in fem-1 could alter male-specific differentiation programs or the timing of AMso division during male maturation required to produce MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].

Narrative: X:13952002 C>T is a missense in alg-1, a core RISC/microRNA factor that controls heterochronic timing and neuronal gene expression; disrupting ALG-1 could mis-time or mis-regulate genes needed for AMso asymmetric division during male sexual maturation [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 23599497, 24244204].
rationale: alg-1 is a core microRNA/RISC component that regulates developmental timing and neuronal differentiation; a missense variant could perturb microRNA-mediated control of genes required for AMso asymmetric division or male maturation that yields MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 23599497, 24244204, 29117550].

Narrative: III:3001342 C>T is a missense in daf-2 (insulin/IGF receptor) that affects neuronal and systemic developmental timing; altered DAF-2 signaling could shift the timing or competence of AMso cells to undergo asymmetric division and produce MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788].
rationale: daf-2 encodes the insulin/IGF receptor that influences developmental timing, neuronal physiology and inter-tissue signaling; a missense could alter the timing or cues for male sexual maturation and thereby affect the division of AMso that produces MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788, 38900346, 39127676].

Narrative: IV:4662815 G>A is a missense in jmjd-1.2, a histone demethylase that modulates Hedgehog-like signaling and axon guidance; epigenetic misregulation may alter transcriptional programs necessary for AMso asymmetric division or male neuronal differentiation [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].
rationale: jmjd-1.2 encodes a histone demethylase that regulates axon guidance and Hedgehog-like signaling in C. elegans; epigenetic dysregulation through a missense could change transcriptional programs required for AMso asymmetric division or glial fate conversion to MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].

Narrative: III:4579586 C>T is a missense in wdr-48, which regulates the deubiquitinating enzyme USP-46 and influences neuronal glutamate receptor abundance; disrupted proteostasis or receptor localization could indirectly impair signaling or cell-surface composition required for AMso asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, 32587090].
rationale: wdr-48 (WD repeat) participates in deubiquitinating enzyme regulation (USP-46) and influences glutamate receptor abundance in neurons; a missense could impair proteostasis or receptor localization in AMso or neighboring cells, indirectly affecting the asymmetric division or survival/differentiation of MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, 32587090].

Narrative: III:2917703 G>A is a missense in a cadherin (cdh-1); cadherins mediate cell–cell adhesion and can influence polarity and fate decisions during development, so a change could alter AMso contact-mediated cues required for asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].
rationale: cdh-1 encodes a cadherin predicted to mediate cell–cell adhesion; proper adhesion and intercellular contacts are important for asymmetric divisions and glial-to-neuron transitions, so a missense could disturb AMso division symmetry or MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].

Narrative: II:14650509 G>A is a missense in unc-52/perlecan, an ECM component influencing dendrite morphogenesis and extracellular interactions; ECM disruption could alter the microenvironment or mechanical cues for AMso asymmetric division, making it a plausible indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29678816].
rationale: unc-52/perlecan is an ECM component required for muscle and neuronal dendrite morphogenesis; misregulation via a missense could alter the extracellular environment or adhesion cues that instruct AMso asymmetric division or MCM positioning [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 8001796, 29678816].

Narrative: III:4691187 C>T is a missense in ppat-1 (purine biosynthesis); metabolic impairment can reduce proliferative competence of progenitors such as AMso, but this is an indirect mechanism and hence lower-priority [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: ppat-1 is involved in purine biosynthesis and cellular metabolism; a missense could impair proliferative capacity of AMso glia required to execute an asymmetric division, making it a plausible but indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:10314117 C>T is a missense in gcy-5, a receptor-type guanylate cyclase expressed in neuronal cilia; altered ciliary signaling from neighboring sensory neurons could modulate intercellular signals that gate AMso division or MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].
rationale: gcy-5 is a receptor-type guanylate cyclase expressed in nervous system cilia; while primarily chemosensory, perturbation could alter neuron–glia signaling or ciliary signaling that affects AMso behavior during maturation [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].

Narrative: II:9749068 C>T is a missense in nos-3, an RNA-binding protein primarily implicated in germline regulation; although likely pleiotropic, the lack of neuronal/glial-specific evidence makes it a weaker candidate for the AMso→MCM phenotype [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: nos-3 is an RNA-binding protein primarily implicated in germline/meiotic events; although less directly linked to AMso asymmetric division, perturbation of an RNA regulator could have pleiotropic developmental effects including on neuronal/glial fate decisions [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:8278445 G>A is a missense in mrpl-10, a mitochondrial ribosomal protein; mitochondrial dysfunction could impair energy-dependent asymmetric division, but this is an indirect mechanism with low specificity to male AMso division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: A missense in a mitochondrial ribosomal protein (mrpl-10) could impair mitochondrial translation and energy supply needed for an AMso cell to execute an asymmetric division; this is a plausible but indirect mechanism [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: III:5802412 C>T is a missense in polq-1 (DNA polymerase theta) involved in DNA repair; while genomic instability can affect dividing cells, a direct, specific effect on AMso asymmetric division and MCM fate is not strongly supported [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: polq-1 (DNA polymerase theta) participates in repair and gap-filling; a missense could modestly increase genome instability impacting dividing AMso cells, but the connection to a specific failure of asymmetric division is indirect [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: III:4799594 C>T is a missense in tag-325, predicted to be a GTPase-activating protein; because small GTPases control polarity/asymmetric division, this is mechanistically plausible though no direct experimental evidence is provided [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: tag-325 is predicted to be a GTPase activator; small GTPase signaling is central to cell polarity and asymmetric division, so a missense could perturb AMso polarity and division symmetry though direct evidence is lacking [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: I:4774285 G>A is a missense in an actin-binding/membrane-organization protein expressed in head ganglion and neurons; cytoskeletal perturbations can disrupt asymmetric cytokinesis or morphological transitions needed for glia→neuron conversion, but direct links are speculative [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: M04F3.5 encodes an actin-binding / membrane organization protein expressed in head neurons and ganglion; a missense could disrupt cytoskeletal dynamics necessary for asymmetric cytokinesis in AMso or for morphological changes required for glia-to-neuron conversion [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:2939242 G>A is a missense in irld-66 (receptor L-domain protein); extracellular receptor alterations could affect signaling that patterns AMso behavior, but the gene lacks supporting functional data so it remains a low-confidence candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: irld-66 encodes a receptor L-domain protein; perturbation could impact extracellular signaling to AMso during male maturation, but evidence is limited and effect is a missense of moderate predicted impact [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: V:19974372 A>G is a missense in a predicted membrane chemoreceptor (srh-173); altered sensory signaling could change systemic cues for male maturation, but the connection to a cell-intrinsic AMso asymmetric-division defect is indirect and low confidence [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: srh-173 is a putative chemosensory GPCR; altered sensory signaling can change neuroendocrine cues for maturation, but this is an indirect and lower-probability mechanism relative to regulators of asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:11452703 C>T is a missense in rsp-2, an RNA-binding regulatory protein implicated in development; disruption could have pleiotropic developmental effects including on dividing glia, but no direct evidence links rsp-2 to AMso asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: rsp-2 is predicted to be an RNA-binding splicing/regulatory factor; missense could have pleiotropic effects on development including glial cell division, but no direct link to AMso asymmetric divisions is available here [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: IV:13640786 C>T is a missense in ugt-22, a UDP-glycosyltransferase; defects in glycosylation can alter extracellular signals or receptor function that might indirectly affect AMso division, but the hypothesis is speculative without supporting data [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: ugt-22 encodes a UDP-glycosyltransferase; metabolic or glycosylation defects could indirectly affect signaling or ECM components involved in AMso behavior, but this is a low-priority, indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:14625250 G>A is a missense in mltn-10, a predicted membrane protein with no further annotation; given the lack of functional information this is a low-probability candidate for the AMso/MCM phenotype [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: mltn-10 is predicted membrane-localized; without curated functional links to glial asymmetric division, a missense is a low-priority indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: V:19515895 C>A is a missense in a predicted serine-type endopeptidase inhibitor; while protease regulation can influence extracellular remodeling during development, there is no direct evidence linking this gene to AMso asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: Predicted serine protease inhibitor (missense). Protease regulation can influence extracellular signaling, but evidence tying this locus to AMso asymmetric division or male-specific neuronal fate is lacking [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:9277239 C>T is a missense in an uncharacterized gene (C01G6.5); without functional annotation or literature this variant is an implausible causal candidate but retained for completeness [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: Uncharacterized gene with a missense variant; without supporting functional data this is a low-probability candidate for AMso asymmetric division failure [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: II:9222055 G>A is a missense in an unannotated gene ZK1067.2; lacking functional information this variant is unlikely to be the primary cause of the AMso→MCM defect but included among low-priority possibilities [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: Missense in an unannotated gene; lacking functional links to glial asymmetric division, considered a low-priority candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

Narrative: III:4691187 C>T is a missense in ppat-1 (purine biosynthesis); metabolic impairment can reduce proliferative competence of progenitors such as AMso, but this is an indirect mechanism and hence lower-priority [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: Included earlier at rank 11 with modest probability; at this lower rank the metabolic role is considered unlikely to be the direct cause of AMso asymmetric division failure but retained as a weak, indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].

rationale: Already scored higher at rank 6; retained here with a minimal residual probability in case of multi-allelic contributions. (See rank 6 rationale.)

rationale: Already considered higher (rank 8) due to neuronal proteostasis role; at this lower residual rank it is an unlikely secondary contributor but kept for completeness. (See rank 8 rationale.)

Narrative: II:11452703 C>T is a missense in rsp-2, an RNA-binding regulatory protein implicated in development; disruption could have pleiotropic developmental effects including on dividing glia, but no direct evidence links rsp-2 to AMso asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
rationale: RNA-binding/splicing factor with wide roles; a low-probability but possible pleiotropic contributor to developmental defects. (See rank 20 rationale.)

rationale: Sensory GPCR variant retained as a distal, low-confidence candidate because altered sensory signaling could modulate maturation cues, but direct mechanistic support is minimal [Effect=missense_variant; non-EMS].
